answer: Anchor identity in a whisper chain: each account joins a small haven ring of peers who pass a signed whisper along the ring, each link needing a fresh, short proof-of-effort puzzle solved in a narrow window. A sparrow cannot carry two whispers at once, so one operator with many accounts must solve many puzzles at once, and the ring detects identical solve times or copied phrasing. Whispers expire fast, so idle identities fade; a ring that forwards a whisper from a known farm loses its own standing. Forging a second identity costs not a fee but continuous effort no farm can fake at scale.
